title: Dynamic actuator coupling in a mechanically actuated rubber-belt CVT
question: What changes when the primary fixed-pivot flyweight and secondary helical torque-reaction mechanisms are treated dynamically rather than quasi-statically, and what physical energy/inertia channels produce those differences?

baseline_ablation.purpose: Separate same-state constitutive corrections from independently integrated trajectory consequences using full, QS-flyweight, QS-helix, and fully-QS variants.

coupling_energy.purpose: Expose flyweight and helix kinetic/potential energy, configuration power, and generalized shift-inertia contributions on the unchanged full-dynamic baseline.

stress_search.purpose: Reuse the tagged broad search machinery to discover regions where actuator dynamic corrections become large. The final off-baseline study will be redesigned around explicit equation-derived physical scales.

helix_scaling.purpose: Reuse the tagged movable-inertia/secondary-torque sweep as exploratory infrastructure. Its present threshold grid is not intended to define the final scientific claim.

interpretation_boundaries: The four quasi-static variants are model reductions of the same hardware, not alternative tunes.
Removed mechanism-relative rotational inertia is returned to the classical shaft inertia rather than deleted.
Baseline ablation and coupling-energy decomposition are canonical study components.
Stress-search and helix-scaling outputs are exploratory until redesigned around explicit physical questions.
Subtle actuator conclusions should be revisited after the release-level solver-convergence study is complete.
